title: Harnessing Context Sensing to Develop a Mobile Intervention for Depression
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mobile phone sensors can be used to develop context-aware systems that automatically detect when patients require assistance. Mobile phones can also provide ecological momentary interventions that deliver tailored assistance during problematic situations. However, such approaches have not yet been used to treat major depressive disorder. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to investigate the technical feasibility, functional reliability, and patient satisfaction with Mobilyze!, a mobile phone- and Internet-based intervention including ecological momentary intervention and context sensing. METHODS: We developed a mobile phone application and supporting architecture, in which machine learning models (ie, learners) predicted patients' mood, emotions, cognitive/motivational states, activities, environmental context, and social context based on at least 38 concurrent phone sensor values (eg, global positioning system, ambient light, recent calls). The website included feedback graphs illustrating correlations between patients' self-reported states, as well as didactics and tools teaching patients behavioral activation concepts. Brief telephone calls and emails with a clinician were used to promote adherence. We enrolled 8 adults with major depressive disorder in a single-arm pilot study to receive Mobilyze! and complete clinical assessments for 8 weeks. RESULTS: Promising accuracy rates (60% to 91%) were achieved by learners predicting categorical contextual states (eg, location). For states rated on scales (eg, mood), predictive capability was poor. Participants were satisfied with the phone application and improved significantly on self-reported depressive symptoms (beta(week) = -.82, P < .001, per-protocol Cohen d = 3.43) and interview measures of depressive symptoms (beta(week) = -.81, P < .001, per-protocol Cohen d = 3.55). Participants also became less likely to meet criteria for major depressive disorder diagnosis (b(week) = -.65, P = .03, per-protocol remission rate = 85.71%). Comorbid anxiety symptoms also decreased (beta(week) = -.71, P < .001, per-protocol Cohen d = 2.58). CONCLUSIONS: Mobilyze! is a scalable, feasible intervention with preliminary evidence of efficacy. To our knowledge, it is the first ecological momentary intervention for unipolar depression, as well as one of the first attempts to use context sensing to identify mental health-related states. Several lessons learned regarding technical functionality, data mining, and software development process are discussed. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT01107041; http://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT01107041 (Archived by WebCite at http://www.webcitation.org/60CVjPH0n).

claims.text: Machine learning models achieved a mean classification accuracy of 60.3% in predicting user location from mobile phone sensor data.
Machine learning models predicting binary categorical social and activity contexts achieved mean accuracy rates ranging from 64.5% to 90.9%.
Machine learning models predicting scale-rated internal states such as mood performed no better than chance.
Participants receiving the Mobilyze! intervention showed significant reductions in self-reported depressive symptoms over 8 weeks.
Participants receiving Mobilyze! showed significant reductions in clinician-rated depressive symptoms over 8 weeks.
Participants receiving Mobilyze! experienced a significant reduction in the likelihood of meeting major depressive disorder diagnostic criteria.
Participants receiving Mobilyze! showed significant reductions in comorbid anxiety symptoms over 8 weeks.

limitations.text: The trial did not include a control condition to account for regression to the mean or confounding factors.
Machine learning prediction models for continuous scale-based states (e.g. mood) achieved poor accuracy, performing no better than chance.
Technical problems including server connectivity loss and rapid battery drain reduced the delivery of prompts and interventions.
The study was conducted with a small sample size of 8 participants.
Traditional Internet interventions for depression suffer from modest outcomes due to high rates of user attrition.

future_work.text: Conduct a randomized controlled trial to confirm clinical outcomes against control conditions.
Adopt cross-platform development frameworks to allow deployment across multiple operating systems and participants' personal devices.
Implement battery management and duty-cycling algorithms to optimize mobile sensor power consumption.
Apply feature extraction, normalization transformations, unpruned regression trees, and ensemble machine learning algorithms to improve continuous state prediction accuracy.
